subject: SLA template and uptime derogation request — GreenLeaf Health
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@greenleafhealth.com>, procurement@greenleafhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Jun 2026 09:12:01 -0700
Subject: SLA template and uptime commitments — draft for GreenLeaf

Hi Sara / team,

Thanks again for the productive call this morning. Attached is the current Redwood SLA template (Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.pdf) for the hosted inference service — this is the standard we propose for the GreenLeaf pilot. Key points in this draft: 99.9% monthly availability baseline for the hosted API, latency SLO (95th p50/p95 numbers called out per route), and a monthly service credit schedule tied to observed availability.

Two quick notes for context:
- We include routine maintenance carve-outs (scheduled maintenance communicated 72+ hours in advance).
- The credit matrix is pro-rata by month and intended to be the primary remediation; one-time operational remedies can be discussed separately.

Please review and let me know any items you need exceptions for. I can pull together a credit worksheet to show the impact to the monthly cap if that helps.

Next step: if you have redlines, please attach them and I can route to our legal and product teams.

Cheers,

Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0142

Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Template_v2.pdf

From: Sara Park <sara.park@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenleafhealth.com
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:03:22 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA template and uptime commitments — draft for GreenLeaf

Monica — thanks for sending this over. We reviewed internally with ops and procurement and have a few exception requests before we can move to legal: 

1) Baseline availability: for our production data plane (critical inference endpoints) we need a guaranteed 99.95% monthly availability or a clearly defined path to a 99.95 commitment within the first 6 months of onboarding. The 99.9 baseline in your draft is a bit low for our regulatory needs.

2) Maintenance carve-outs: we will accept scheduled maintenance but need a separate carve-out for batched retrain/inference windows that can cause elevated latency — those should not be counted the same as routine maintenance.

3) Monthly credit cap: we cannot accept an open-ended or very high monthly credit that exceeds 8% of monthly services spend. Can you confirm a hard cap and show us a worked example of how credits would apply?

I've attached our initial redlines (GLH_redlines_v1.docx) with inline comments on the latency section and credit cap language. Will need the credit calculator (or sample numbers) before our CFO signs off.

Best,

Sara Park
Director, Cloud Operations | GreenLeaf Health
sara.park@greenleafhealth.com
Attachment: GLH_redlines_v1.docx

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@greenleafhealth.com>, procurement@greenleafhealth.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 09:34:10 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template and uptime commitments — draft for GreenLeaf

Sara — appreciate the clear redlines and context. Quick responses inline below and a proposed path forward.

1) Baseline availability:
- We can commit to a phased approach: 99.9% at contract signature with a guaranteed uplift to 99.95% within 90 days of production readiness, contingent on GreenLeaf completing the recommended operational onboarding checklist (traffic shaping, prefix caching enabled, routing policy applied). We will include the uplift timeline in the commercial SOW.

2) Maintenance carve-outs:
- We can add a separate "experimental batch window" carve-out limited to X hours/month that GreenLeaf can schedule; any unscheduled batch-impacting maintenance will be subject to post-incident review. We'll capture this as a defined carve-out clause rather than lumping into routine maintenance.

3) Monthly credit cap:
- We understand the need for a hard cap. Our standard template uses a sliding cap tied to monthly invoice (example in the attached credit_calculator.xlsx). Per your ask, we can offer a firm maximum of 8% of monthly services spend as the aggregate credit cap for the hosted API. The attached calc shows examples at $50k and $200k monthly spends.

Attached: credit_calculator.xlsx (worked examples). I've also flagged the precise language edits we'll propose to legal (and will incorporate your GLH_redlines_v1 where they align).

If this sounds workable I'd like to schedule a 30-minute call with Karthik (solutions) and Ben (commercial lead) next week to lock timelines and update the SOW. Suggested slots: Tue 6/16 10:00-10:30 PDT or Wed 6/17 14:00-14:30 PDT.

Thanks — I want to be pragmatic here and get you to legal with a clean set of mutual concessions.

—Monica
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Attachment: credit_calculator.xlsx

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Sara Park <sara.park@greenleafhealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 15:47:05 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template and uptime commitments — draft for GreenLeaf

Sara / Monica — looping in commercial perspective. Two clarifications / a small counterproposal from our side to keep risk balanced for both parties: 

• Uptime uplift path: Monica's 90-day uplift to 99.95% is acceptable provided GreenLeaf signs the onboarding checklist and traffic profile thresholds in the SOW. We will include a 30-day performance verification window where we measure real-world traffic before the uplift is final.

• Monthly credit cap: we can agree to an 8% hard cap for hosted API, but request the cap be applied at the invoice-line (hosted inference) level and not across a blended Redwood invoice that includes professional services / integrations. This prevents cross-subsidizing unrelated spend.

• Experimental batch carve-out: to make the carve-out operationally manageable, propose a default allowance of 12 hours/month scheduled batch window (GreenLeaf to provide calendar entries 7 days prior). Unscheduled batch-impacting events beyond that will be reviewed and may be eligible for partial credits after RCA.

If these three points are okay I will have legal prepare the limited redline set and we can move to an electronic DocuSign review. Monica — please capture these in the SOW addendum and include the HubSpot Deal link when you send the next draft.

—Ben
Commercial Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Sara Park <sara.park@greenleafhealth.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenleafhealth.com, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 10:12:30 -0400
Subject: Re: SLA template and uptime commitments — draft for GreenLeaf

Thanks — that helps. We can accept the staged uplift (99.9 -> 99.95 in 90 days) tied to the onboarding checklist and the 30-day verification window. The 8% cap applied to the hosted inference invoice line is acceptable — please make that explicit in the SOW addendum.

Agreed on the 12 hours/month scheduled batch window — procurement will provide the preferred monthly window after signature.

Next steps: Monica — please send the SOW addendum with the uplift schedule, invoice-line credit cap language, and the batch carve-out wording. We'll have legal run a quick review and aim to return final redlines within 72 hours. Once legal has the SOW we'll be ready to route to the CFO.

Sara
Director, Cloud Operations | GreenLeaf Health
